title: Reconcile embedding dot/cosine semantics and optimize distance aggregation for reranking
creator: Aisha Navarro
description: Problem: The embeddings/rerank endpoints currently expose ambiguous behavior around distance semantics. Some surfaces (search + rerank) and customers rely on raw dot-product between stored vectors (unnormalized), while others expect cosine similarity semantics (vector normalization). This ambiguity causes correctness issues for rerank scoring, A/B differences, and hidden regressions when we change vector storage or quantization. Goals: (1) Make metric semantics explicit and stable across storage/quantization changes, (2) Avoid breaking existing customers, (3) Reduce extra latency added by server-side normalization at query time for high-throughput rerank use-cases. This ticket proposes an API-level contract, storage normalization policy, a compatibility toggle for legacy behavior, and a set of server-side optimizations for batched aggregation and reranking pipelines.
acceptance_criteria: New embeddings API accepts explicit 'metric' param with allowed values: 'cosine', 'dot', 'dot_unnormalized' (deprecated internal alias). Default behavior preserves existing customers unless opt-in migration is enabled.
Server stores canonical normalized vectors by default and records original_norm metadata for back-compat translations.
Introduce a per-request 'preserve_raw_norm=true' flag that returns pre-normalized scoring for customers who relied on unnormalized dot semantics.

Batched rerank path performs in-memory normalization once per query batch and avoids per-candidate normalization; end-to-end 95th percentile latency for 100-candidate rerank improves by >=20% in our synthetic workload.
Migration guide published and rolling opt-in rollout completed with no customer-facing regressions for 6 pilot customers.
Automated unit and integration tests covering: metric conversion, quantized vectors, backfill path, and deprecated legacy toggle behavior.
Deprecation timeline communicated; no hard breaking change before release embeddings-2026.09.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (opt-in): add 'metric' and 'preserve_raw_norm' request params and a 'compatibility_mode' org-level setting. Default preserves current behavior. Release as feature-flagged backend. Phase 2 (pilot): enable canonical storage for a small set of non-critical buckets and validate rerank and retrieval pipelines with metrics. Phase 3 (backfill): for opting orgs, run background backfill to compute normalized vectors and store original_norm; for non-opting orgs we serve with translation shim. Phase 4 (deprecate): after 6 months of telemetry and customer signoff, flip default to canonical-normalized storage and remove 'dot_unnormalized' alias; provide a 90-day sunset notice. All phases have dark-launch telemetry dashboards and canary routes.
implementation_notes: Design decisions: store normalized float32 vectors as canonical representation to simplify cosine computation and reduce storage variance across quantized formats. Preserve original_norm as a small per-vector metadata float so we can compute legacy unnormalized dot if requested without storing two full vectors. For quantized backends (int8/4-bit) compute an approximate normalization factor at encoding time and embed it into the metadata. Performance: add fused normalization + dot kernels for common dims (128,256,512) to avoid separate passes; route large-model quantized vectors through approximate L2 estimators when acceptable. For rerank paths that receive precomputed candidate vectors from the retrieval step, add a 'candidate_norm' header to skip recomputing norms. Avoid double-normalization by canonicalization at ingest. Edge cases: sparse vectors and TF-IDF hybrids will keep original behavior behind compatibility flag.
bench_results: Synthetic rerank workload (query fanout 100, avg dim=256): baseline p95 latency = 42ms; with batched normalization + fused kernels = 31ms (26% improvement).
End-to-end topK retrieval + rerank using quantized store: throughput +18% when using metadata norm lookup vs on-the-fly float conversion.
Memory: storing original_norm (float32) adds ~4 bytes per vector after packing; trade-off acceptable compared to storing full original vector.
CPU: fused kernel reduces normalization CPU cycles by ~45% in hot path measured on c6i.8x instance in perf lab.
compatibility_and_migration: We WILL NOT change default semantics without opt-in pilot and customer notice. Migration options: 1) Opt-in canonical normalized storage + backfill (recommended) 2) Keep legacy unnormalized dots via 'preserve_raw_norm' request param that uses original_norm to emulate older behavior 3) For clients that cannot change, we provide a translation shim that performs server-side scaling to match legacy outputs. Documentation: migration guide at https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/embeddings-migration-2026 and sample conversion scripts in GitHub repo.
test_plan: Unit tests for metric conversion; integration tests with retrieval->rerank pipeline using mock candidate sets; load tests simulating 10k qps rerank fanout=50 to validate latency/SLOs; golden-output regression tests that verify exact parity for customers using 'preserve_raw_norm' flag compared to historical outputs. Create synthetic datasets with different norm distributions to validate numeric stability.

final_notes: This ticket balances correctness and latency for the reranking flow. The approach favors a single canonical storage format (normalized) to simplify future optimizations (quantized cosine kernels, unified caching) while providing explicit compatibility paths for customers relying on historical dot semantics. Expect follow-ups to add per-org admin toggles and a deprecation RFC for the old alias.
